summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, morbid obesity, and a recent hospitalization for cholangitis and DVT was readmitted due to low-grade fevers at her rehabilitation facility. She reported decreased appetite and constipation but denied other infectious symptoms. Evaluation revealed no evidence of infection, with negative blood cultures, a clean dialysis site, and no pneumonia on chest X-ray. Her subtherapeutic INR was corrected with warfarin adjustment, and a follow-up leg ultrasound showed stable, non-worsening DVT. Constipation resolved with bowel regimen, and appetite returned. She remained afebrile, with stable labs and no complications. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to continue warfarin, monitor INR, manage constipation, and follow up on dialysis and oxygen use.
